droid-monkey attacked this Android app with a real-world fault and it failed. Fix the root cause.

## What happened
Attack `permission_revoke` (permission_revoke): Grant a permission through the app, revoke it the way Settings does, come back and use the feature again.
Steps: [{"tap": "scan_coupon"}, {"accept_permission": true}, {"settle": 3}, {"fault": "revoke_permission", "permission": "android.permission.CAMERA"}, {"restart_to_screen": true}, {"tap": "scan_coupon"}, {"settle": 4.0}]
Result: crashed: java.lang.SecurityException: validateClientPermissionsLocked:1848: Caller "com.shubhasai.monkeymart" (PID 16510, UID 10240) cannot open camera "1" without camera permission
Crash: java.lang.SecurityException @ com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui.CouponScanner.open(CouponScanner.kt:44)
  at com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui.CouponScanner.open(CouponScanner.kt:44)
  at com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui.CouponScannerKt.ScanCouponButton$lambda$9$lambda$8$lambda$7(CouponScanner.kt:77)
  at com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui.CouponScannerKt$$ExternalSyntheticLambda2.invoke(D8$$SyntheticClass:0)

## Diagnosis
Root cause: CouponScanner remembers camera access in a SharedPreferences boolean that is set once after a grant (CouponScanner.kt:37, written in ScanCouponButton at :66) and never cleared. The Scan button gates on that flag alone (CouponScanner.kt:76-77), so after Settings revokes CAMERA the app still believes it has access and calls CameraManager.openCamera directly (CouponScanner.kt:44), which throws SecurityException. The fault invalidates the cached grant, but the app never rechecks the real permission state.
Fix approach: Drop the persisted flag and make the gate ask the system: use ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission(context, Manifest.permission.CAMERA) == PERMISSION_GRANTED in hasCameraAccess. If it is not granted, launch the RequestPermission contract instead of opening the camera. Also wrap openCamera in try/catch for SecurityException and surface a status message as a last-resort guard against races with revocation.
Evidence: app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CouponScanner.kt:33-34 - hasCameraAccess returns a SharedPreferences boolean, not the live permission state; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CouponScanner.kt:36-38 - rememberCameraGranted persists camera_granted=true and nothing ever clears it; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CouponScanner.kt:66 - the permission callback writes the flag after a successful grant; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CouponScanner.kt:76-77 - the button opens the camera when the stale flag is true, with no permission check; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CouponScanner.kt:44 - cameras.openCamera throws SecurityException once CAMERA is revoked; the crash frame matches this line; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CouponScanner.kt:79 - the request-permission path exists but is unreachable after revocation because of the stale flag; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutScreen.kt:74 - the checkout screen renders ScanCouponButton(), so the crash happens on the checkout_form screen

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CouponScanner.kt

## Regression test
Instrumented test in src/androidTest, class CouponScannerPermissionTest: grant CAMERA, open checkout_form, revoke CAMERA with `pm revoke` or UiAutomation, then tap the scan_coupon tag. Assert no SecurityException is thrown and that the request-permission path runs (the status text is 'Camera permission is needed to scan coupons' or the system permission dialog appears). This fails before the fix because the stale flag calls open() directly, and passes after because hasCameraAccess checks the live permission.

## Rules
- Fix the root cause in the files above with the idiomatic Android approach. Keep the change small and focused.
- Add exactly one regression test file under app/src/test (JVM unit test, preferred) or app/src/androidTest
  (instrumented), using only test libraries the project already has (see app/build.gradle.kts). It must fail on
  the old code and pass on the fixed code.
- Do not change build files or add dependencies. Do not touch unrelated code. Do not commit.
- Before you finish, call the compile tool on your test ('unit' or 'instrumented') and fix every error it reports.
- When done, reply with one short paragraph: what you changed and the test class name.

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. - update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

package com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui

import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxSize
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxWidth
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.padding
import androidx.compose.foundation.rememberScrollState
import androidx.compose.foundation.text.KeyboardOptions
import androidx.compose.foundation.verticalScroll
import androidx.compose.material3.Button
import androidx.compose.material3.Card
import androidx.compose.material3.CircularProgressIndicator
import androidx.compose.material3.MaterialTheme
import androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField
import androidx.compose.material3.Text
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalContext
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.platform.testTag
import androidx.compose.ui.text.input.KeyboardType
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import androidx.lifecycle.viewmodel.compose.viewModel
import com.shubhasai.monkeymart.data.OrderRepository
import com.shubhasai.monkeymart.data.ProductRepository
import com.shubhasai.monkeymart.data.priceLabel

@Composable
fun CheckoutScreen(
    productId: Int,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    vm: CheckoutViewModel = viewModel(),
) {
    val product = ProductRepository.cached(productId)
    val context = LocalContext.current
    val orders = remember { OrderRepository(context) }

    val placedId = vm.orderId
    if (placedId != null) {
        Column(modifier.fillMaxSize().padding(24.dp).testTag("order_confirmed"), verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp)) {
            Text("Order placed 🎉", style = MaterialTheme.typography.headlineSmall)
            Text("Order $placedId is on its way to ${vm.city}.", modifier = Modifier.testTag("order_id"))
        }
        return
    }

    Column(
        modifier = modifier
            .fillMaxSize()
            .verticalScroll(rememberScrollState())
            .padding(16.dp)
            .testTag("checkout_screen"),
        verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp),
    ) {
        if (product != null) {
            Card(Modifier.fillMaxWidth()) {
                Row(Modifier.padding(16.dp), horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.SpaceBetween) {
                    Text("${product.emoji} ${product.name}", style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium, modifier = Modifier.weight(1f))
                    Text(product.priceLabel(), style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium, modifier = Modifier.testTag("checkout_total"))
                }
            }
        }

        Text("Delivery details", style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium)
        CheckoutField("Full name", vm.name, { vm.name = it }, "field_name")
        CheckoutField("Email", vm.email, { vm.email = it }, "field_email", KeyboardType.Email)
        CheckoutField("Phone", vm.phone, { vm.phone = it }, "field_phone", KeyboardType.Phone)
        CheckoutField("Address", vm.address, { vm.address = it }, "field_address")
        CheckoutField("City", vm.city, { vm.city = it }, "field_city")
        CheckoutField("Pincode", vm.pincode, { vm.pincode = it }, "field_pincode", KeyboardType.Number)

        ScanCouponButton()

        Button(
            onClick = { vm.placeOrder(orders, productId) },
            enabled = vm.isComplete && !vm.placing,
            modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth().testTag("place_order"),
        ) {
            if (vm.placing) CircularProgressIndicator(Modifier.testTag("placing_order")) else Text("Place order")
        }
    }
}

@Composable
private fun CheckoutField(
    label: String,
    value: String,
